# F4, F1, F6 and F11, and the one red that proves all four

Four more of the twelve are closed. Red 178 and green 179 are the round: each new
test fails against the mutation its own finding describes, which is the only way to
show a test that was written after the code has teeth.

**F4, the registry omitting the checks with no configuration file.**
`harness/no-live-marketplace-host` is the twenty-third rule, and it is proven the way
the hook runs it: `_run_harness` calls the check rather than spawning an interpreter,
over a fixture whose connector test fetches a live Bol URL. `harness/rules.py` had
said in as many words that the harness's checks were in the set because they run in
the same hook, while the registry carried neither, so the comment is corrected too.

Two things fall out. `secrets.marketplace_hosts` now skips `rules/fixtures/`, because
that directory is the one place in the tree where a violation is supposed to live and
the other four tools ignore it by scope already; without that line the fixture would
fail the repository's own lint, and `test_the_fixture_tree_is_not_read_by_the_check_it_proves`
is what holds it. And **gitleaks stays out of the registry deliberately**: a fixture
proving it would have to carry a string gitleaks detects, and the hook runs
`gitleaks protect --staged` on every commit, so nobody could commit the fixture
without an allowlist weakening the control the rule is about. The reason is written in
`rules.py` where the next person to ask will look. If Ruud would rather have the entry
with an allowlisted fixture, that is a decision and not an oversight.

`test_the_registry_carries_a_rule_for_each_tool_the_set_runs` now reads
`RUNNER_FOR_TOOL` instead of a list written in the test, which is F4's own rule
candidate: a tool that runs with no entry fails that test from now on without anybody
remembering to edit it.

**F1, the weekly report's rule loop.** Two tests in `ReportTest` run
`harness report --week` as the command and read the loop out of the rendered report
and out of the payload: the caught list naming a registry rule, the rules-added line,
and a candidate that recurred with no rule. Deleting either the `--week` branch in
`cli.py` or the argument to `reporting.render` fails them, which is what the finding
asked for. The tests plant their ticket under the project's own id, because
`ticket_figures` walks `docs/tickets/*.md` and a planted journal with no ticket file
is a ticket the weekly report cannot see; that is worth knowing for any later test of
this command.

**F6, `rule_candidate` on the return path.** Three tests in `ReturningFindingsTest`:
a medium finding with nothing in the field is refused, a malformed value is refused,
and a low finding still owes nothing. Wrapping the check in `if resolved:` now fails
two of them.

**F11** is one sentence in `docs/harness/workflow.md`: it said the whole set runs in
the pre-commit hook, and knip runs in CI, because a dead export is a property of the
whole import graph.

## What is left

F7, the knowledge graph, which is `graphify update .` plus a decision about the
post-commit hook CLAUDE.md describes and this repository does not have. And the
judgement on the four low findings, F8, F9, F10 and F12: whether each is this
ticket's or a follow-up's. Record 173 says what each one takes, and record 175 what
the three ticket-file findings came to.

Nothing in this round touched a slice's production files except `harness/rules.py`
and `harness/secrets.py`, so the replay the next review needs is the one in
`.harness-drafts/replay2.sh`, unchanged.
